source.author: verg
source.text: Postquam altum tenuere rates, nec iam amplius ullae apparent terrae, caelum undique et undique pontus, tum mihi caeruleus supra caput astitit imber, noctem hiememque ferens, et inhorruit unda tenebris.
source.text_original: Postquam altum tenuere rates, nec iam amplius ullae / apparent terrae, caelum undique et undique pontus, / tum mihi caeruleus supra caput astitit imber, / noctem hiememque ferens, et inhorruit unda tenebris.
source.text_english: After the ships had held the deep, and no lands now appeared any more, sky on every side and sea on every side, then above my head stood a dark-blue rain-cloud, bringing night and winter, and the wave bristled with darkness.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: et quia paululum non tam desiui a uitiis, quam coepi uelle desinere, nunc me nouis diabolus retibus ligat, nunc noua inpedimenta proponens maria undique circumdat et undique pontum, nunc in medio constitutus elemento nec regredi uolo nec progredi possum.
reuse.text_original: et quia paululum non tam desiui a uitiis, quam coepi uelle desinere, nunc me nouis diabolus retibus ligat, nunc noua inpedimenta proponens maria undique circumdat et undique pontum, nunc in medio constitutus elemento nec regredi uolo nec progredi possum.
reuse.text_english: And because I have not so much ceased from vices as begun to want to cease, the devil now binds me with new nets, now, setting new obstacles before me, he surrounds me on every side with sea and on every side with the deep; now, placed in the middle of the element, I neither want to go back nor can I go forward.
